- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent highs.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >78) — add 2–5% buffer to avoid undershoot.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment — adjust by smoothing 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (0.3–0.5), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves after strong upward momentum — cap downward revisions at 2% unless sentiment confirms bearish shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — add 1–3% upward adjustment if last 5 days show rising trend + sentiment > 0.5.
- If sentiment drops sharply after forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in prior momentum.
